title: L2-ARCTIC manually annotated subset
why_promising: Primary read English production from 24 non-native speakers across six L1 backgrounds. Public Lhotse documentation identifies 3,599 manually annotated utterances, approximately 9,458 phone segments excluding silence, 1,673 phone substitutions, 456 deletions and 90 additions; the manual subset has corrected word/phone alignment rather than relying on the corpus-wide forced alignment.

title: Mixed language processing increases cross-language phonetic transfer in Bengali-English bilinguals
why_promising: Primary bilingual production experiment with openly available OSF materials/data/code. Ten speakers produced English target vowels in mixed and nonswitched conditions across two tasks; recordings were manually segmented/annotated in Praat and F1/F2 were measured at five trajectory points (5%, 15%, 25%, 35%, 45%) for 2,333 retained target tokens ([ʌ] 1,137; [æ] 1,196). This is directly useful for trajectory-preserving vowel/coarticulation analyses.
open_question: Enumerate OSF file tree and download token-level data; verify whether the deposit contains raw Hz values, normalized values, boundary timestamps and/or audio. Preserve all five timepoints and task/context/word/speaker identifiers; do not collapse trajectories to midpoints.
